versions.short: The bill would take dyslexia out of the general definition of specific learning disability in the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act and give it its own separate definition in that law. Under the new definition, dyslexia would mean an unexpected difficulty in reading for someone who has the intelligence to read much better, most often caused by trouble with the sounds of spoken language, which affects speaking, reading, and spelling. The bill would also require schools and other agencies deciding eligibility for or providing services under that law to give equal access to children from low-income families, children from families with low socioeconomic status, and children who are limited English proficient.
